text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - Bund futures continued their strong rise, breaking the previous contract high and threatening the 101.00 level -- an advance that only a few weeks ago seemed out of the question. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.03, up 0.36 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - gilts ended a rollar-coaster day near session highs as bargain hunters snapped up cheap stock battered by renewed inflation concerns. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-28/32, up 30/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures followed Bunds and U.S. Treasuries higher late in the day to settle at a new contract high but traders said there were no major players behind the move and the contract could slip back on Friday. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 127.66, up 0.24 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Bond futures started slightly easier but soon picked up to show small gains, with the market's attention on the nation's key 1997 budget which is making its way through parliament. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.66, up 1.04 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury prices opened lower on Thursday before a data troika due in early trade. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 115-3/32, up 12/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.44 percent.

JAPAN - Key December Japanese government bond futures ended slightly higher, as the Trust Fund Bureau of the Ministry of Finance said it would continue to buy JGBs from the market. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 124.45, down 0.09 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Activity in Thursday's Eurobond market spanned a wide range of currencies. Fannie Mae issued a $500 million five-year global bond with a call after two years. Ford units launched both Danish crown and dollar issues. Investors were also offered Ecu, Australian dollar, guilder, lira and rand bonds. Russia was due to start the London leg of its roadshow on Friday, with hundreds of investors expected to attend. St Petersburg said it was close to receiving ratings.
